No one thinks less of the F-35 than I. And I've been saying we should pull the plug for literally 10 years. This isn't a program of the 2000's. It is a program of the 1980s. It was obvious by the time the prototypes flew that the plane would not be operational within it's window of usefulness as a weapons system. Remember the DOD started dreaming up this project before the fall of the Soviet Union. The glacially slow governmental RFP was issued in the 1990s.

One of the reasons the program is such an uncharacteristically huge disaster is because almost none of the assumptions made in 1988 are valid today: from a massive conventional war with the Soviets in eastern europe to autonomous systems being "buck rogers" stuff 200 years in the future. Because of this, and the ONLY thing I will say in Lockheed's defense, the requirements have changed continuously - especially for the software. But of course this just shows how flawed the contract is. There was no workable plan for upgrading the plane.

It is also worth mentioning that this is not the first time the DOD has embraced the folly of a plane that does lots of things mediocrely OK-ish. The F-111 was another failed fantasy that in its day was just as big a disaster as the F-35. They didn't learn a damn thing from that. If we do not TURN OFF the F-35 program and sell them for scrap they will not learn anything from this either.
